questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Besides experiencing a new culture and trying to live abroad on the other side of the world, the academic opportunities at UniMelb also appealed to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Definitely worth it. You learn a lot about yourself and you get to broaden your horizon.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. You already get a lot of information through mail prior to arriving and there is a welcome day and an orientation week before the teaching period begins, where you'll get all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I felt like I got assistance with almost everything. There is definitely more assistance in general than at UCPH, where you are expected to complete various things more independently.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I don't feel like there was anything where I didn't get the necessary help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find a room in an apartment on my own. I heard from a lot of other students that they had a very hard time finding something though and therefore ended up in student accommodation. It seems like the rental prices in Melbourne have gone up a lot since covid.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cheaper, but on the other hand it would also mean that you live a bit outside the CBD and a bit further away from campus compared to the student accommodations. Whether that's a good or a bad thing is a personal matter I guess.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a huge supply of student accommodation in the CBD, but it is very expensive. Especially if you compare to "kollegier" in Denmark. As already mentioned, finding accommodation on your own is rather difficult though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't stress about your courses before getting down to Melbourne as there is plenty of time to choose which courses you want to enroll in. The deadline for choosing courses is way later than in Copenhagen. If I remember correctly, it's not before like 2-3 weeks into the semester where you have to decide which courses to choose. This means you can attend classes the first two weeks and get a feel for whether you're interested in a particular course or not.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After getting the pre-approval from UCPH you have to check whether the specific course has pre-requisites. If it does, you have to email the professor and prove that you meet those pre-requisites. After this, you can enrol in the course. There is plenty of help how to do this at "Stop 1", which you will hear about when you get down there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of help for enrolling in your courses at "Stop 1", so don't stress about it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I basically got all courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again: Don't stress too much about it before getting down there as you will have plenty of time to enroll in the courses. It's a good idea to have a look in the handbook prior to arriving though and see what kind of courses are offered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally the same level as at UCPH, but of course depending on the subject. However, the workload during the semester was bigger at UniMelb since you have to hand in assignments and hold presentations which account for a certain percentage of your grade. This is very different to UCPH, where you mostly just have one big exam in the end. However, this did make the final exam period less stressful and intense than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same as at UCPH with both lectures and tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Macroeconometrics (ECOM90007)
Quantitative Analysis of Finance II (ECON90010)
Derivative Securities (FNCE90011)
Data Analysis for Finance (FNCE90083)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you're interested in learning about bayesian techniques in macroeconometrics then I'd definitely recommend Macroeconometrics (ECOM90007). As far as I know there is no course at UCPH covering bayesian econometrics, so this is quite a unique opportunity. However, the workload in this course is very big. I think I devoted around 80% of my study time to this course. The course is very rewarding though and the lecturer (Tomasz Wozniak) is great.

Other than that I'd also recommend Derivative Securities (FNCE90011). It is not math heavy (compared to what we are used to at UCPH), but is rather focusing on the intuition behind pricing various derivatives.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any unexpected cost, however the general price level was just higher than expected I guess.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Rent - More expensive than in Copenhagen
Groceries - Probably same price level as in Copenhagen
Take away food - A bit cheaper than in Copenhagen
Beer - Way more expensive than in Copenhagen
Coffee - Way cheaper than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a club for almost anything, so there is plenty of opportunity to engage in various activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the surf club and participate in one of the surf camps - you'll have a great time. Further, I could also recommend the mountaineering club as they also offer some great trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy all the events in Melbourne and explore a bit of Victoria. (Great Ocean Road, Grampians National Park, Wilsons Promontory National Park)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy as Australia obviously also is a western society and therefore not too hard to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join one of the aforementioned clubs. You will meet a lot of the local students there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any differences I found challenging - just different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very open and talkative and not as reserved as Europeans, which was really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go travelling before and/or after the semester
2. 
3. Bring warm clothes as Melbourne gets cold in the winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy a bike. Public transport is quite expensive in Melbourne, but the bike lanes are pretty good actually.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all over the world and being able to perform academically in a foreign country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing the big workload during the semester while also trying to have as much fun as possible.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
